calls.head: Stars collide: Aho vs. Knies
calls.body: At home, the Hurricanes keep sending Aho’s line (Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rod Brind'Amour has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Blue Jackets’ first line is Knies, Coyle and Olivier.

calls.head: The Hurricanes should drive the play
calls.body: The Hurricanes have been the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blue Jackets around the middle. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Blue Jackets’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Carolina hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Carolina’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 39, against their usual 104 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 100 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Kochetkov wins his first nine, a Hurricanes record
paras: Jordan Martinook struck first for the Hurricanes late in the first, and Logan Stankoven made it 2-0 early in the second. Mark Jankowski stretched the lead to 3-0 just 16 seconds into the third, and that one stood up as the winner. Denton Mateychuk and Kent Johnson scored just under three minutes apart early in the period to cut Carolina’s lead to 3-2, but the Hurricanes held on.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Blue Jackets hit two posts and came up a goal short. Pyotr Kochetkov made 24 saves for the Hurricanes, and Jet Greaves stopped 24 of 27 at the other end. Kochetkov has won all nine of his starts this season, the longest winning run to open a season by any goalie in franchise history, one more than Frederik Andersen (2021-22). He also tied the franchise record for straight wins in one season, shared by Cam Ward (2008-09) and Brandon Bussi (2025-26). No NHL goalie had opened a season with this many straight wins since Jack Campbell won his first eleven in 2020-21. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Seth Jarvis, by our Swing measure. The Canes improved to 11-2-2, still first in the NHL in both points and points percentage, while the Blue Jackets dropped to 5-6-0, seventh in the Metropolitan.
